newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Annan proposes halting cut in U.N. Macedonia force.
newsitem.headline: Annan proposes halting cut in U.N. Macedonia force.

text.p: Secretary-General Kofi Annan recommended on Tuesday suspending a planned 300-man reduction in the 1,050-member U.N. force stationed in the former Yugoslav republic of Macedonia, because of current unrest in neighbouring Albania.

When the Security Council last November renewed the mandate of the U.N. Preventive Deployment Force (UNPREDEP) in Macedonia until May 31, it also called for a phased reduction in its size, to be completed by April 30.

UNPREDEP, which includes some 440 U.S. troops and a similar number from Nordic countries, was originally deployed to prevent conflicts elsewhere in the former Yugoslavia from spilling over into Macedonia.

But in a letter to the president of the Security Council, Annan said: "Recent developments in Albania and the resulting situation of lawlessness and banditry in certain parts of that country have demonstrated that stability in the Balkan region remains extremely fragile."

While there appeared to be "no imminent danger of the problems in Albania spilling over to the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia, the current crisis is a source of great anxiety in that country," he said.
Macedonia's foreign minister, in a letter last month, underlined the seriousness of the situation and asked that the reduction in UNPREDEP's military component be suspended, Annan added.

When the force began dismantling its observation posts along the borders with Yugoslavia at the end of March, this was "misperceived and resulted in immediate criticism of UNPREDEP in the local press." The troop drawdown was temporarily suspended but would have to be resumed soon if the April 30 deadline was to be met.

"In the light of the above, and on the basis of the advice of my special representative, I recommend that the Security Council approve the suspension of the reduction of the UNPREDEP military component until the end of the current mandate on May 31, 1997," Annan said.
